title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S lies over S_0 = Spec Z[1/2]. Grothendieck is building a 'Legendre-type' description of elliptic curves through the quotient P^1-bundle E/{±1} and its four branch points.

(1) Data. Let p: J -> S be a finite étale cover of degree 3. Then O_S^J := p_*O_J is locally free of rank 3, and its trace O_S^J -> O_S is surjective (in the split case tr(e_1) = 1). Its kernel V_J is locally free of rank 2. Put Σ_J = P(V_J) (EGA convention, Proj Sym), a genuine P^1-bundle over S. Evaluation at the points of J gives rank-one quotients of V_J. This embeds J as an étale degree-3 divisor D_J ⊂ Σ_J, and Σ_J^* := Σ_J \ D_J; the notation is used on the next page. Since PGL_2 acts simply transitively on ordered triples of distinct points, (Σ_J, D_J) is the universal model: any P^1-bundle with an étale cubic divisor D is canonically isomorphic to (Σ_{D}, D_{D}).

(2) Twists. From the previous page, M ↦ M^♮ = M ∧^{μ_4} Q_0 = M ⊗ L_0. Here Q_0 is a fixed μ_4-torsor over Z[1/2] and L_0 is an invertible sheaf with L_0^{⊗4} trivial. Squaring sends Q_0 to the μ_2-torsor μ_4^* (the primitive 4th roots, i.e. the cover Z[1/2,i]). Hence (M^♮)^{⊗2} = M^{⊗2} ∧^{±1} μ_4^*.

(26) defines T_∘ := O_{Σ_J}(1)^♮, so T_∘^{⊗2} ≅ O(2) ∧ μ_4^*.

(27) uses the relative Euler sequence for a P^1-bundle: T_{Σ/S} ≅ O(2) ⊗ det(V_J)^{∨}. Also det V_J ≅ det p_*O_J, the line attached to the sign character of the S_3-torsor of J. That is ω_J ∧^{±1} O_S, where ω_J is the quadratic (discriminant) étale cover associated with J; it is self-dual. Hence T_∘^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J} ∧ (μ_4^* ∧ ω_J).

(3) Elliptic curves. For E/S elliptic, J := ({}_2E)^* = E[2] minus the origin is an étale cubic cover (28). The quotient E/{±1} is a P^1-bundle whose branch divisor is 0 ∪ J. By the rigidity in (1) it is canonically ≅ Σ_J, with J -> D_J and the zero section going to a section t of Σ_J^* (29). Since the double cover is ramified at 0 with local equation s = z^2, one gets T_{E,0}^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ_J,t} (30, next page).

The purpose (next page) is a 'jacobian rigidification' K: T_{E,0} ≅ O(1)^♮_t whose square matches (27)/(30) via a trivialisation α of μ_4^*∧ω_J. Since -1 acts by -1 on T_{E,0}, such a K kills the ±1 automorphism. The goal is to describe M_{1,1} over Z[1/2] (with rigidifications) in terms of (J, t ∈ Σ_J^*, α). Over k these become the pairs (t, i), t ∈ P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, i ∈ μ_4^* of the previous page: a canonical, base-free form of the Legendre λ-family.
errors: No real mathematical error. The twisting by ω_J in (27) depends on identifying det V_J with ω_J ∧ O and on the Euler-sequence convention; since ω_J is a μ_2-torsor, the dual/non-dual ambiguity is harmless.
Notational inconsistency with the next page: (27) has μ_4^* ∧ ω_J, while (32)-(33) write μ_2^× ∧ ω_J. Probably μ_4^* (or a slip) is meant there.
Canonicity of (29) needs the remark (implicit here) that a P^1-bundle with an étale cubic divisor has no nontrivial automorphisms fixing the divisor pointwise.

ideas.what: Rank-2 bundle V_J = ker(trace: p_*O_J -> O_S) for an étale cubic cover, and Σ_J = P(V_J) as the canonical P^1-bundle containing J as a divisor
ideas.modern_name: standard (trace-zero) representation of S_3 twisted by the S_3-torsor; universal P^1 with three marked points
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (twisted forms of P^1 with 3 points)

ideas.what: Tangent bundle of Σ_J ≅ O(2) twisted by the discriminant quadratic cover ω_J (det of the trace-zero bundle = sign character)
ideas.modern_name: relative Euler sequence plus the discriminant torsor of a cubic étale algebra

ideas.what: Twisting by a μ_4-torsor Q_0 over Z[1/2] whose square is the μ_2-torsor μ_4^* of primitive 4th roots of unity
ideas.modern_name: twisting by a 4-torsion line bundle / μ_4-gerbe-type twist

ideas.what: E/{±1} ≅ Σ_{E[2]^*} canonically, and T_{E,0}^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}
ideas.modern_name: Legendre form / level-2 description of elliptic curves via the x-coordinate double cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre, Jacobi; modern stacky versions by Deligne, Fulton–Olsson and others

ideas.what: Jacobian rigidification: an isomorphism of T_{E,0} with a twisted O(1)_t, compatible on squares, killing the ±1 automorphism
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of M_{1,1}[1/2] removing the μ_2 inertia, a canonical form of the Legendre λ-line with μ_4 twist data
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related to rigidification (Abramovich–Corti–Vistoli) and Legendre/level-2 descriptions

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a canonical, base-free description of elliptic curves over Z[1/2] by data (étale cubic J, section t of Σ_J \ D_J, μ_4-twisted tangent rigidification). It is a Legendre-type presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2] modulo ±1 via the S_3-twisted λ-line plus a μ_4-torsor Q_0 over Z[1/2]. This fits his Esquisse-era interest in U_{0,3} and the Teichmüller tower. The specific μ_4-twist bookkeeping (Q_0, ♮ and ♭ operations) does not seem to appear in this form in the literature, though the underlying mathematics is classical.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives an arithmetic, descent-friendly model of M_{1,1}[1/2] over the stack of cubic étale algebras. This is mildly relevant to explicit Picard-group and arithmetic-fundamental-group computations around M_{1,1} and the λ-line. It is mostly a repackaging of known Legendre/level-2 theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but essentially classical construction (Legendre form, E/±1 as a twisted P^1 with three marked points, discriminant twist of the tangent bundle). It is recast functorially over Z[1/2] with an unusual μ_4-torsor twist. The interest is in the presentation and its link to the λ-line program, not in a new result.
transcription_corrections: (25) marginal note: V_J(O_S) is the kernel of the trace map O_S^J --(tr)--> O_S, with O_S^J = p_*(O_J), p: J -> S. The '(tr)' is written above the arrow.
Line after (25): reads roughly 'd'où un module inversible O_{Σ_J}(1), [et] un module' rather than 'et un module inversible ... un module'.
(26) and (27): the subscript is T_∘ (T with a small circle) on Σ_J; the second isomorphism in (27) is T_{Σ_J} ∧_{±1} (μ_4^* ∧ ω_J).
'Si maintenant E est une courbe elliptique sur la base S, on lui associé[?]' — the word before (28) looks like 'associé' rather than 'revêtement'.
(28): J = ({}_2E)^* rev. étale cubique de S. (29): E/(±id_E) ≃ Σ_J.
